clue.text: Sort of party backed by great fictional character

indicators.note: backed means the party word is read from back to front

parts.note: a stag party is a bachelor's last night out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist's grand creation is linked to some kind of party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition nods to the novel The Great Gatsby, so 'great' belongs to the definition rather than describing the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the title figure of Fitzgerald's novel The Great Gatsby.

clue.text: Plucky lyrist's first to join an Asian ensemble

parts.note: game means brave, plucky

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the lyre player word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bold harpist leads off by joining an Eastern band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plucky' suggests plucking strings, but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamelan is a traditional Indonesian orchestra of gongs and metallophones.

clue.text: Kindling catches on

definitions.meaning: small sticks used to light a fire
in British slang, to twig is to realise or catch on

explanation.definitionFit: Small sticks are fire kindling, and to twig means to grasp, so it also means catches on.

clue.text: European houses to New Englander

indicators.note: houses means contains, so the European word holds the little word

parts.note: a Bosnian is a European from Bosnia

explanation.surface: A European offers accommodation to someone from New England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the containment signal, and 'to' gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bostonian comes from Boston, the chief city of New England.

clue.text: Have no truck with tender? Endlessly one moves wagons

parts.note: to have no truck with someone is to shun them

indicators.note: read literally as 'without END', so those three letters come out of the word tender

explanation.surface: Railway talk: a locomotive refusing to deal with its tender while shifting freight cars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' does not trim the ends of tender; it removes the run END from it, leaving TER. 'truck' and 'tender' both pretend to be railway vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A shunter is a small locomotive or worker that moves railway wagons around a yard.

clue.text: Mountainous areas in the middle of Russia on the radio

indicators.note: radio operators spell letters with the phonetic alphabet, in which S is Sierra
the middle of the country name is its two central letters

explanation.surface: A broadcast about mountain ranges in central Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of Russia is SS, which a radio operator would say as 'Sierra Sierra', giving SIERRAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierras are jagged mountain ranges, so they are mountainous areas.

clue.text: Trouble in college with group of students

parts.note: being up means in residence at a university
a set is a class group of pupils

explanation.surface: Bother at university involving a class.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to upset or disturb them.

clue.text: Hard worker going over green in which horse was present

parts.note: to work like a Trojan is to work very hard

indicators.note: going over means turning back, so the word for green reads in reverse

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A diligent worker crosses the lawn where a horse was standing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'horse' is the wooden horse of Troy; 'going over' turns RAW into WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The war against Troy featured the famous wooden horse hiding Greek soldiers.

clue.text: Correct bit of metal piping goes outside

indicators.note: the shrill word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: piping means shrill, as a reedy voice is

indicators.note: bit of takes just the opening letter of metal

explanation.surface: A section of metal pipework fitted externally sorts out the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of' takes M from metal, and 'goes outside' wraps REEDY round it: RE-M-EDY.
explanation.definitionFit: To remedy a fault is to correct it.

clue.text: Box camera originally taken by volunteer

indicators.note: originally points to the initial letter of camera

parts.note: to offer is to volunteer

explanation.surface: A box camera, initially accepted by someone who stepped forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box camera' looks like a single item, but 'Box' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffer is a strongbox or chest for valuables.

clue.text: Criminal doesn't aim for prison

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook who misses his target still ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' signals rearranging the letters of DOESNTAIM. MAIDSTONE is a county town in Kent with a well-known prison, HMP Maidstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is the name of an English jail, so the town name stands for a prison.

clue.text: Shop closing early before mass attack

indicators.note: a shop shutting before time loses its last letter

parts.note: a store is a shop
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A shop shuts ahead of time before a crowd surges in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing early' cuts the final E from STORE, giving STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to attack it in a sudden assault.

clue.text: Catcher in novel also first for Salinger

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging
first for picks out the opening letter of the author's name

explanation.surface: A reference to The Catcher in the Rye, Salinger's famous novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges ALSO plus S, the first letter of Salinger. The surface leans on Salinger's novel The Catcher in the Rye.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope loop thrown by cowboys is used to catch animals, so it is a catcher.

clue.text: Oldest measure for horse — from its mouth?

parts.note: the oldest child is the first-born
horses are measured in hands, units of four inches

explanation.surface: A question about the earliest way of sizing up a horse, with a nod to its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'straight from the horse's mouth', meaning information from a direct source.
explanation.definitionFit: News straight from the horse's mouth is direct, unmediated information, which is what firsthand means.

clue.text: Smarter rabbit comprehending one

indicators.note: comprehending in its sense of including means the chatter word holds the numeral

parts.note: in British slang to rabbit on is to natter, chatter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cleverer rabbit grasps a single idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is not the animal but British slang (rabbit and pork, talk) for chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means neat and smart in dress, so the comparative means better turned out.

clue.text: Catch line that's knotted with a sort of hitch

indicators.note: a tangled line has its letters knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A fishing line tied up and snagged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's knotted' rearranges CATCHLINE; a technical hitch is a mechanical fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical hitch is a common phrase for a mechanical or equipment fault.

clue.text: Spread bad news about Turkey

indicators.note: about here means one piece surrounds the other
bad suggests something spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Ill tidings from Turkey are being circulated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the letters of news to SEWN, and 'about' wraps that round the Turkey abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means scattered about, the past participle of spread in that sense.

clue.text: Boater, possibly, may be seen in Durham

definitions.meaning: a boater straw hat is an example of clothing worn on the water
the city of Durham stands on a river named the Wear

explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a cathedral city in north-east England; a boater is a flat straw hat traditionally worn for rowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing for rowing is river garb, while the city of Durham stands on the River Wear.

clue.text: Light fitment in the old days (after second century)

indicators.note: after puts the old-times word behind the two abbreviations

parts.note: once means formerly, in the old days

explanation.surface: A lamp fitting from long ago, dated from the second century onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a date range, but it just orders the pieces: ONCE comes after S and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A sconce is a wall bracket holding a candle or lamp, a kind of light fitting.

clue.text: Bore, extremely unpopular, stopping over

indicators.note: stopping as in filling a gap, so the edges of unpopular plug the middle

parts.note: over means finished, ended

indicators.note: extremely picks the two outermost letters of unpopular

explanation.surface: A deeply disliked bore halting proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a noun for a dull person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is a past tense verb: to have borne something is to have endured it.

clue.text: Nuts deserve to be cut off

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Mad people deserve to be shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like a noun but signals rearranging DESERVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something severed has been cut off cleanly, as a limb or a tie.

clue.text: Don't go to bed — sleepyhead exercises!

parts.note: to sit up is to stay awake late
read as the head of sleepy, its first letter

explanation.surface: A plea to stay up, aimed at a drowsy person, about workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleepyhead' is split as sleepy's head, the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises done by raising the body from lying.

clue.text: Given inferior status, daughter displayed strong feelings

parts.note: to emote is to show emotion theatrically

explanation.surface: A downgraded daughter made a fuss about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be demoted is to be lowered in rank.

clue.text: Hoot about being taken in by swindle

indicators.note: the swindle word swallows the short word for about

parts.note: a scam is a swindle
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Laughing about being conned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hoot' means something hilarious, not an owl's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot and a scream are both informal words for something very funny.

clue.text: Treaty or pact oddly ignored by state capital

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters keeps only the even ones of the word pact

explanation.surface: An agreement or deal is snubbed in strange fashion by a seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Concord is the capital of the US state of New Hampshire; 'or' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Marshal may be tall?

definitions.meaning: to marshal is to arrange or organise
a tall ... is a demanding request

explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops is to arrange them, and a hard request is called a tall order.

clue.text: True capital of Mayan kingdom

parts.note: real means true, genuine

indicators.note: capital in its sense of capital letter, so the first letter of Mayan

explanation.surface: The genuine seat of power in an ancient Mayan kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' suggests a city but means the opening letter, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Top group didn't fast before noon

parts.note: to have eaten is the opposite of fasting
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: Elite people had breakfast in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-team is the first-choice group, the best people available.

clue.text: Delicacies half-cooked for Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged
half takes the first five of the ten letters of the delicacies word

explanation.surface: Fine foods only partly cooked for a medieval Spanish knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes DELIC from Delicacies, and 'cooked' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar was the Castilian warrior known by the title El Cid.

clue.text: Stand for show again?

definitions.meaning: to stand for something is to symbolise or act for it
split as ..., to present or display once more

explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to stand for something; split with a hyphen it means present anew.

clue.text: Woman from the loony left? Not so!

parts.note: loony suggests wild, and the closing 'Not so!' flips it to its opposite, mild
politically, a left-winger is called a red

explanation.surface: Is this lady one of the crazy socialists? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: The loony left would be WILD RED; 'Not so!' tells you to take the opposite of loony, so MILD RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Patient's beginning 7 — not finishing drugs before operation

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the patient word
not finishing drops the final letter of the cure word

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a cure or correction

explanation.surface: Medical: the start of a patient's treatment is incomplete before surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is a cross-reference to the answer of 7 down; the definition reads pre-med as short for premedication.
explanation.definitionFit: Premed is medication given to calm a patient before an operation.
